text:
The neighbor would most likely recover in negligence for the property damage. I don't accept the team note: trespass requires intent to cause the entry, or knowledge with substantial certainty that it would happen, and intending to work with flammables isn't intending smoke to cross onto the neighbor's land. An accidental fire that sent smoke over the boundary doesn't meet that test, and a nuisance claim would also be weak because a single accident isn't a continuing interference. A spark igniting gasoline and oil residue left on the floor points to a failure of reasonable care, and the discolored home is actual damage.

CONFIDENCE: 66
